A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison despite the changed title and organization.

before.justification: v2 reports original unlearning and relearning experiments on TOFU, WMDP, Harry Potter tasks and synthetic name sequences, including quantitative results and qualitative examples.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and reports additional data-relevance tests, control experiments and comparator results.

M1.justification: The auxiliary-data finetuning procedure and Algorithm 1 are unchanged despite renaming targeted relearning as benign relearning. The RMU-specific zero-initialization adaptation already appears in v2 Section 7 and moves to v4 Appendix E.

E1.justification: The benchmarks and core tasks remain unchanged. v4 adds limited input scenarios: Japanese text, female-name sequences and gibberish in the synthetic experiment, and German and gibberish relearning text for WMDP (Section 6 and Appendix C.5.5).

E2.justification: The copyrighted-text comparison expands from GA, GD and NPO in v2 Table 4 to include KL and SCRUB in v4 Figure 5. Although already evaluated on WMDP, these two methods are new comparators within the copyrighted-text experiment.

E3.justification: v4 Figure 3 adds zero-unlearning checkpoints. Appendix G extends controls without prior domain-memorization finetuning to synthetic and copyrighted-text tasks, and Appendix C.5.5 adds a GA-based MCQ relevance experiment. The existing evaluation sample sizes, metrics and stated training settings are retained.

E4.justification: v4 adds substantial validation of the relearning interpretation: Section 6 and Appendix C.5.5 test dependence on relearning-data relevance, while Appendix G extends the auxiliary-data-only control beyond the TOFU experiment already present in v2. These address whether recovery depends on related information and whether auxiliary training alone explains success.

E5.justification: Both versions report aggregate scores without seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. Additional checkpoints and synthetic token repetitions are experimental conditions, not newly reported independent runs.

E6.justification: v4 adds relevance and pretrained-control results in Tables 5, 7 and 9, plus copyrighted-text results for KL and SCRUB, with relearned Rouge-L scores of 0.51 and 0.44. It also replaces v2 Figure 4's duplicated retention panels with distinct MT-Bench scores in Figure 7; the reported original Zephyr score changes from 5.92 to 7.33. Existing WMDP forget, LoRA and RMU results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The threat-model definitions, forget-loss equation and baseline objectives are retained. v2 Appendix E becomes v4 Appendix F, and metric definitions move to Appendix I without substantive mathematical changes. Neither version supplies new theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: v4's abstract and introduction explicitly diagnose current approximate unlearning as output obfuscation, strengthening v2's emphasis on susceptibility to relearning. This is limited strengthening: v2's conclusion already states that many optimization-based heuristics fail to truly remove memorized information, and the central contribution remains unchanged.

C2.justification: v4 adds interpretation of data-relevance experiments and notes that strongly related relearning data may be unavailable. Appendix G extends the argument against learning evaluation answers solely from auxiliary text. It also mentions unverified inference-time applicability; existing model-choice, RMU, metric and guardrail limitations remain.

D1.justification: v4 Section 5 clarifies that the synthetic forget set uses common male names, where v2 Section 6 specifies only a subset of names. This is a small disclosure refinement, not evidence of a changed experiment. Existing hyperparameters, data-generation and filtering prompts, and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: v4 discusses subsequent low-MI finetuning findings by Łucki and colleagues and Deeb and Roger, distinguishes recovery after pruning in Lo and colleagues, and connects the synthetic experiment to memorization studies. These additions refine the existing positioning rather than redefine it.

P1.justification: The narrative is substantially reorganized: related work moves from Section 2 to Section 8, RMU experiments move to Appendix E, and the algorithm and detailed metric explanations move to Appendices H and I. The title, terminology, abstract and introduction are also revised.

P2.justification: v4 substantially changes the displays and layout: the copyrighted-text table becomes an expanded bar chart, forget and retain panels are separated, heatmaps gain zero-unlearning columns and revised scales, and new analysis tables appear. Appendix J adds an alternative line-plot presentation of Figure 3.

improvement.justification: v4 strengthens validation through relevance ablations and controls beyond the TOFU check already in v2, expands the copyrighted-text comparison, and replaces duplicated retention panels with distinct MT-Bench results. These improve evidential support and reporting accuracy. The broader obfuscation claim still requires qualification beyond the tested settings, making the net improvement useful but limited.
